hints.title: Use one trigonometric quantity
hints.body: The angles are all 2x. Use cos2(2x)=1−sin2(2x) and then put u=sin(2x) to turn the equation into a quadratic.
hints.recap: The identity sine squared plus cosine squared equals one can reduce a mixed equation to one variable.
hints.pitfall: The identity uses the same angle in both terms; retain 2x throughout.
hints.pause: Substitute and rearrange so that the coefficient of u squared is positive.

recall.reminder: The identity sine squared plus cosine squared equals one can reduce a mixed equation to one variable.

hints.title: Solve for the trigonometric value
hints.body: Solve the quadratic exactly, using a factorisation or the quadratic formula. Check every resulting value against the range of sine.
hints.recap: An algebraic value of a trigonometric quantity can correspond to several angles.
hints.pitfall: Do not confuse the number of quadratic roots with the number of angular solutions.
hints.pause: Derive the permitted sine values and find their reference angles.

recall.reminder: An algebraic value of a trigonometric quantity can correspond to several angles.

hints.title: Double the interval before listing angles
hints.body: Double both ends of the stated x interval. Use the period of sine to extend your first-turn angles across the resulting full interval before converting back.
hints.recap: Solve for the inner angle on its full transformed interval, then return to x.
hints.pitfall: The largest value of 2x is not itself the answer for x.
hints.pause: List every allowed inner angle, divide by two and select the greatest original angle.

recall.reminder: Solve for the inner angle on its full transformed interval, then return to x.

solution:
1. Reduce to a quadratic. Replace cos2(2x) by 1−sin2(2x). Rearrangement gives sin2(2x)−3sin(2x)+34=0.

2. Solve for the sine value. (sin(2x)−32)2=0, so sin(2x)=32.

3. Use the full interval. On 0∘≤2x≤720∘, the solutions are 2x=60∘,120∘,420∘,480∘. Hence x=30∘,60∘,210∘,240∘.

Answer F. The largest value is 240∘.
